title: Pseudorandom batch behavior troubleshooting - Felix Moreno
content:
Quick brain dump after today's triage (notes to self). High-level: intermittent p99 token latency spikes that correlate with small variances in observed batch sizes. Hypothesis: pseudorandom batch boundary timing + KV cache eviction interplay leads to occasional cache misses and kernel switching overhead.

Observed symptom set:
- Production: short bursts (~10-30s) where p99 token latency jumps from ~45ms to 180-300ms across model-xl-8x pool.
- Spike frequency: ~3-6x per day per node pool; seems slightly higher during lower traffic windows (midnight-3am UTC).
- Correlation: when average batch size dips below 2.1 tokens/req for 10s windows, next 2000 tokens show elevated latency.

Immediate reproduction steps (local / staging):
1) Use bench-client v0.23 with synthetic short prompt mix (lengths 8-24 tokens) and poisson arrival (lambda tuned to get mean concurrency ~4).
2) Enable --inject-jitter 0.15 to mimic observed jitter.
3) Run against staging runtime with KV cache metrics enabled (env: RUNTIME_KV_METRICS=1).

Quick commands (staging):
- start bench: ./bench-client --model model-xl-8x --concurrency 4 --prompt-mix short --inject-jitter 0.15 --dur 600
- tail metrics: kubectl logs -f deploy/runtime-staging --selector=app=runtime | grep "kv_cache"
- collect perf: sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30; sudo perf script > perf.st

Small snapshot of bench results (staging run 2026-03-12 15:14):
- mean latency (token): 52ms
- p95: 72ms
- p99: 260ms (episodes: 12 spikes over 10m)
- avg batch size: 1.9 tokens/req during spikes, 3.4 otherwise

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Stochastic batching algorithm sometimes produces very small aggregate batches (1-2) causing kernel launch overhead to dominate. Kernel selection path triggers a different quantized kernel (fast path vs fallback path) because input length distribution crosses threshold at runtime (race).
2) KV cache eviction heuristic is reactive: when batch sizes are tiny, a new request path causes a cache miss and a synchronous refill that stalls token generation for the whole microbatch.
3) Network jitter + inter-node routing occasionally routes to a node with a cold NVCache leading to CUDA context warm-up (~100ms).
4) GC/alloc in runtime C++ thread pool triggered by burst of tiny allocations (less likely but saw one sample in perf).

Quick evidence notes:
- KV metrics show a ~1.2x increase in cache_miss_rate during spike windows.
- Perf samples show an increased percentage of time in cudaMemcpy + cuLaunchKernel during spikes (consistent with kernel launch overhead).
- No obvious memory pressure in node metrics (GPU mem stable).

Minimal experiments to run tomorrow (priority order):
- EXP-A: Force deterministic batching (no jitter) for 30m to confirm whether jitter is necessary for spike reproductions. Config: runtime.batch.strategy=deterministic; bench inject-jitter=0.
- EXP-B: Change kernel selection threshold to always prefer small-batch-optimized kernel for inputs < 16 tokens (feature flag: runtime.kernel.force_small_batch=true) — run for 60m and observe p99.
- EXP-C: Temporarily disable KV synchronous refill path (fall back to async background refill) in staging to observe spike behavior. Gauge regressions on quality (none expected, this is cache-only).
- EXP-D: Add ephemeral sampling to trace one spike and capture full stack + env of serving node (collect /proc, lsof, cuda driver version) and post to PR for follow-up.

Things to add to the PR (if EXP-B reduces p99):
- Microbenchmark showing kernel latency across batch sizes 1..8 (include wall-clock & CUDA timings).
- Unit test for kernel selection logic covering boundary conditions (len==15/16).
- Telemetry: log kernel_choice tag and batch_size in trace spans for 72 hours post-rollout.

Open TODOs (me):
- [ ] Run EXP-A on staging (assign to self) and collect data by EOD tomorrow.
- [ ] Create small microbench harness for kernel path timing; aim for <1 day hookup.
- [ ] Add a lightweight span tag kernel_choice to tracing (discuss with SRE about cardinality). See linked PR attempt: github PR #982 (WIP).
- [ ] Sync with Marta on KV heuristic changes — schedule 20m call.
- [ ] Draft rollback plan for force_small_batch flag (how to revert and throttle).

Notes from quick pairing with Ivy (today):
- Ivy saw a case where batcher produced a microbatch of 0.9 avg tokens/req because a single huge prompt came through and starved other requests in the microbatch window. She suggested increasing max_wait_ms slightly for low-qps windows.
- We discussed adding short-term smoothing: keep a 5s rolling average batch size and avoid switching kernel paths if the rolling average doesn't change by >0.5. Potential pitfalls: smoothing can add latency during real load changes.

Potential risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Forcing small-batch kernel might hurt throughput under heavy load (path not optimized for large batches). Mitigation: Feature flag + rollout 10% traffic then ramp. Add per-route gating.
- Risk: Telemetry cardinality explosion from kernel_choice tag. Mitigation: sample 1% of requests or only tag error/spike traces.

Random troubleshooting notes (to capture ephemeral thoughts):
- Remember to check driver upgrades around midnight; one node had a different minor driver patch that correlated with a single-day increase in spikes last month. Add driver version to node tags in traces.
- Check if dedicated pool autoscaler had any recent config changes (autoscale cooldown). Jira RT-1443 might have context.

Edge-case idea for follow-up (low priority):
- Explore prefix caching policy that prioritizes requests based on estimated remaining tokens to avoid tiny-batch starvation. Could reduce microbatch variance for short prompts.

Links/refs:
- Related PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/982
- Slack convo (archived): https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C0123AB45/p1647382920000
- Jira: JIRA-RT-1443 (kv-cache eviction tuning)

Summary (one-liner): Try deterministic batching + force small-batch kernel in staging to see which lever reduces p99 spikes; collect kernel_choice telemetry and KV miss metrics to disambiguate root cause.

Notes-to-self end. Keep quick record here before formalizing the postmortem.

-- Felix
